Certain products are final sale because they are customized, hygienically sensitive, perishable, or otherwise
unsuitable for ordinary resale.
Typical final-sale products include: - personalized engraving, - custom furniture, - monogrammed items, - opened
hygiene products, - perishable goods, - digital downloads, - certain clearance items marked “Final Sale.”
Final-sale status does not remove the customer’s ability to report a defective, damaged, or incorrect item where
the applicable defect or fulfillment policy provides a remedy.
A customer should always be toldwhy a standard return is unavailable and which alternative process, if any,
remains available.

Loyalty-Points Redemption Policy
Nimbus Rewards points can be earned on qualifying purchases and redeemed for eligible discounts or benefits.
9.1 Redemption Rules
• Minimum redemption: 500 points.
• Standard conversion: 100 points =€1 discount.
• Maximum points redemption: 30% of eligible merchandise subtotal.
• Points cannot normally be exchanged for cash.
• Points cannot be transferred between customer accounts.
• Points cannot be used to pay taxes or certain regulated fees.
• Some promotional items may be excluded.
The redemption interface displays the maximum number of points that can be applied to a particular order.
9.2 Points Expiration
Unless a campaign states otherwise, reward points expire12 months after the month in which they were
earned. A customer may see pending points before they become redeemable.
Cancelled or returned purchases may reverse points that were originally awarded for those purchases.
9.3 Refunds and Loyalty Points
When an order paid partly with points is refunded, the cash portion is refunded according to the original payment
method and eligible points are normally returned to the customer’s rewards balance.
If points were earned from the purchase being returned, those earned points may be removed.
9.4 Promotional Multipliers
During a 2x or 3x points campaign, the campaign-specific terms determine which products qualify. Promotional
points may have a separate expiration date if explicitly stated.

Page 1
 Nimbus Commerce — Order Merge and Consolidation
 Policy
Document type: Internal customer-support policy | Version: 1.0 | Effective date: 7 September 2026
Purpose: This document defines the rules for customers who want two or more separate Nimbus Commerce
orders to be combined into one shipment after checkout. It introduces a distinct operational scenario for retrieval
testing and should be treated independently from return, cancellation, address-change, partial-shipment, and
standard delivery policies.
1. Scope
Order consolidation is an optional warehouse-handling request. It does not convert multiple orders into a single
commercial order, invoice, payment transaction, loyalty transaction, or return record. Each original order keeps its
own order number and financial history.
2. When a Merge Request May Be Submitted
A customer may request consolidation when all candidate orders satisfy the following conditions:
Condition
Requirement
Fulfillment
All orders must be fulfilled by Nimbus Commerce's own warehouse network.
Warehouse
Orders must currently be assigned to the same fulfillment center.
Status
Every order must be paid and not yet handed to a carrier.
Destination
Shipping address must match exactly at the order-record level.
Packaging
No order may already have entered final packing or carrier-label creation.
3. Cases That Must Not Be Consolidated
Support must reject the merge request if any candidate order is seller-fulfilled, already manifested to a carrier,
assigned to different warehouses, placed on fraud-review hold, contains a regulated shipping restriction, or has a
destination mismatch. Orders containing digital-only products are also excluded because they do not enter the
physical shipment workflow.
4. What Consolidation Changes
If warehouse operations approve the request, eligible physical items may be packed together under one shipping
container. The system records the consolidation event against every participating order. Original order totals, tax
calculations, coupon applications, payment authorizations, and item-level identifiers remain unchanged.
The customer should not be told that the orders have been 'merged into one order.' The approved wording is that
the orders have been 'consolidated for shipment.' This distinction is important because future returns, refunds,
warranty claims, and invoices continue to reference the originating order.
5. Shipping Charge Treatment
Consolidation does not automatically recalculate shipping fees.
